claims.claim: Spoken / sighted Nantucket off Nantucket (20th 6 PM)
claims.citation: New York Herald, 22 July 1866, p. 9, col. 5
claims.verbatim:
Steamship Hermann (Brem), Wenke, Bremen July 8, via
Southampton 10th, 11 PM, with mdse and 685 passengers, to
Oelrichs & Co. Had westerly winds during the passage.
11th inst, 7 AM, off Cowes, passed steamship New York,
hence for Bremen; 13th, ship Zephyr, bound E; 19th, lat 42
15, lon 62, Tonawanda, bound W; 20th, 6 PM, off Nantucket,
steamship City of Cork, hence for Liverpool.

claims.citation: New York Herald, 26 July 1866, p. 2, col. 6
claims.verbatim:
Ship Ceres (of Yarmouth), Humphrey, Shields, May 23[?],
with coal, to master. 2d inst lat 44 43, lon 50 18[?], was boarded
by a boat from schr Emily Elliott, of Provincetown, one
month out; had 200[?] quintals fish; also by a boat from schr
Orilolo[?], of same place, 1 month out, 300[?] quintals; 21st, lat
40[?] 48, lon 66[?] 40[?], signalized steamship City of Cork, hence for
Liverpool. Have been 22 days W of the Banks with light
WSW winds; saw no ice.
